speaker: Doctor
text: Does the swelling appear in other joints as well, and have you noticed any unusual bruising on his skin or frequent nosebleeds? Given the family history, I'd like to order a coagulation panel; REQUEST TEST: PT, PTT, and Factor VIII levels.

text: RESULTS: Inspection reveals swelling only in the right knee with no other swellings or deformities elsewhere; no unusual bruising or frequent nosebleeds are noted in the examination. speaker: Doctor
text: Given the hemarthrosis and prolonged ACT, does the boy have a history of bleeding after vaccinations or minor cuts, and did the father experience similar bleeding issues? REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the prolonged ACT and hemarthrosis in a young male with a family history, I need to check his hemoglobin and platelet count immediately to assess for anemia or thrombocytopenia. REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and reticulocyte count.

text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count results: Hemoglobin is 12.2 g/dL, Hematocrit is 36%, Leukocyte count is 7,300/mm³, Platelet count is 200,000/mm³, and Reticulocyte count is 1.2%.

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal platelets and hemoglobin but a prolonged ACT and confirmed hemarthrosis, I suspect a clotting factor deficiency like Hemophilia A or B. Since Factor VIII and IX levels were unavailable in previous requests, I will now specifically order those assays and von Willebrand factor tests. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII, Factor IX, and von Willebrand Factor levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the Factor VIII, Factor IX, and von Willebrand factor levels are normal, this effectively rules out the most common inherited clotting disorders like Hemophilia A or B.
